quote: Proposition 3. Let X ~ MEG(eta, beta_1) and Y ~ MEG(eta, beta_2). If beta_2 > beta_1, then X <=LR Y.
family: modified exponentiated family MEG(eta, beta) with cdf F(y) = phi(beta)[(1+G(y; eta))^beta - 1], phi(beta) = beta(2^beta - 1)^{-1}, beta > 0
compared: two MEG variables with common eta, ordered shape beta

quote: Corollary 1. Let X ~ MEG(eta, beta_1) and Y ~ MEG(eta, beta_2). If beta_2 > beta_1, then 1. X <=HR Y and X <=ST Y. 2. E(X^k) <= E(Y^k) for all k in Z+.
compared: two MEG variables ordered in beta

conclusion.direction: X <=_hr Y and X <=_st Y; also E(X^k) <= E(Y^k)

ambiguity: Consequence of Proposition 3 via LR => HR => ST (equation 11).

quote: Proposition 4. Let X1 and X2 be two Poisson-MEG mixtures with cdfs H1(x; beta_1) and H2(x; beta_2), respectively. If beta_2 > beta_1, then X1 <=LR X2.
family: Poisson-MEG mixture: X | Lambda = lambda ~ Poisson(lambda), Lambda ~ MEG(eta, beta)
compared: two Poisson mixtures with MEG mixing parameters beta_1 < beta_2

hypotheses.formal: Lambda_1 <=_lr Lambda_2 by Proposition 3; Poisson family TP2 in lambda

ambiguity: Proof via TP2 property of Poisson and Theorem 1.C.17 of Shaked and Shanthikumar.

quote: Corollary 2. Let X1 and X2 be two Poisson-MEG mixtures with cdfs H1(x; beta_1) and H2(x; beta_2) and hrfs h1 and h2, respectively. If beta_2 > beta_1 then 1. X1 <=HR X2 and X1 <=ST X2. 2. E(X1^k) <= E(X2^k), for k in Z+.
compared: two Poisson-MEG mixtures ordered by beta

conclusion.direction: X1 <=_hr X2 and X1 <=_st X2; moment ordering E(X1^k) <= E(X2^k)

quote: Corollary 3. Let X ~ MEG(eta, beta_1) and Y ~ MEG(eta, beta_2). If beta_2 > beta_1, then 1. X_{r:n} <=ST Y_{r:n} for r = 1, ..., n. 2. E(X_{r:n}) <= E(Y_{r:n}), provided the expectations exist.
model: other: order statistics of iid samples
family: MEG(eta, beta); random samples of size n
compared: rth order statistics of samples from MEG(beta_1) vs MEG(beta_2)

conclusion.direction: X_{r:n} <=_st Y_{r:n} for all r; E(X_{r:n}) <= E(Y_{r:n})

ambiguity: Follows from X <=_st Y via Theorem 4.4.1 in [22].
